gap: No result ChatGPT got states that these portable CarPlay dash cams run off a 5 V USB-C feed from the 12 V socket. Rexing's parking mode for the CPDuo-686 needs a separate $29.99 'FM Smart Hardwire Kit' wired to the fuse box with ACC detection, and both makers tie FM audio to their own power adapter (Rexing sells 'FM' chargers and hardwire kits for the CPDuo line, and Carpuride warns that a non-original charger 'will affect the FM transmission performance'). So the hardwiring that parking recording needs also has to use the maker's own FM-capable cord.
standout_why: I opened jadocam.com's 'Best Dash Cam with Apple CarPlay (2026)'. It mentions parking mode only as something to 'pay for' and names a 'hardwire kit or cigarette lighter' without explaining what either does. It says nothing about the FM transmitter living in the power cord or about needing a brand-specific FM hardwire kit. ChatGPT's answer only warns about rear cameras that work only in reverse. The cited Road & Track page and the Car and Driver roundup refused automated fetches, and dashgearlab.com failed with a TLS certificate error, so I could not check those three. Score held at 2 rather than 3 for that reason.
decides: Anyone who wants the dash cam to cover the parked car, or who has an older car with no AUX or Bluetooth and so depends on FM, should budget for the maker's own FM hardwire kit. That is $29.99 at rexing.com for the CPDuo-686 and siblings. A generic fuse-tap kit or a USB port may power the screen but lose FM audio and won't trigger parking mode. Rexing publishes a parking-mode kit for this line; in the Carpuride listing text I could read, none was offered for the W903. So the Rexing CPDuo-686 fits a parking-recording buyer better, and the Carpuride W903 fits a buyer who only needs recording while driving.
